canDo.en: I can introduce my family and other people and say simple things about them.
canDo.bg: Мога да представя семейството си и други хора и да кажа прости неща за тях.

body.en: Use "he" for a man or boy and "she" for a woman or girl. For things that belong to them, use "his" (for a man) and "her" (for a woman). Careful: in English "his" or "her" depends on the owner, not on the thing. So it is "his sister" (the sister of a man) and "her brother" (the brother of a woman). Bulgarian works the same way ("неговата сестра", "нейният брат"), so ask yourself: whose is it?
body.bg: Използвай "he" за мъж или момче и "she" за жена или момиче. За нещо, което е тяхно, използвай "his" (негов — на мъж) и "her" (неин — на жена). Внимавай: на английски "his" или "her" зависи от притежателя, а не от предмета. Така че е "his sister" (сестрата на мъж) и "her brother" (братът на жена). На български е по същия начин ("неговата сестра", "нейният брат"), така че се питай: чие е?

examples: This is my brother. He is ten.
This is my mother. She is a doctor.

body.en: To introduce someone, say "This is my…": "This is my dad." Use "is" with he, she and one person (he's, she's). Use "are" with they and two or more people (they're). English always needs a subject: in Bulgarian you can say "Лекарка е", but in English you need "She is a doctor". Notice "a" before jobs: "She is a doctor", "He is a teacher".
body.bg: За да представиш някого, кажи "This is my…": "This is my dad." (Това е баща ми.) Използвай "is" с he, she и един човек (he's, she's). Използвай "are" с they и двама или повече души (they're). В английския подлогът е задължителен: на български можеш да кажеш "Лекарка е", но на английски трябва "She is a doctor". Обърни внимание на "a" пред професиите: "She is a doctor", "He is a teacher".

meaning.en: Used to show or introduce a person or thing near you.
meaning.bg: Това, този, тази — за да покажеш или представиш някого.

meaning.en: A man or boy (as the subject).
A woman or girl (as the subject).
Two or more people or things.
meaning.bg: Те — за двама или повече души или неща.

meaning.en: Me and other people.
Belonging to a man or boy.
meaning.bg: Негов, негова, негово — на мъж или момче.

meaning.en: Belonging to a woman or girl.
meaning.bg: Неин, нейна, нейно — на жена или момиче.

meaning.en: A group of people like parents, children, brothers and sisters.
A woman who has a child.
A man who has a child.
An informal word for "mother" (American English; British: "mum").
An informal word for "father".
A mother or a father.
A boy or man with the same parents as you.
A girl or woman with the same parents as you.
The mother of your mother or father.
A person you like and know well.
A person who helps sick people.
A person who designs and builds machines, roads or computer systems.
Nice and friendly to other people.
More than a little; it makes a word stronger.

Inside a place: in Sofia, in a house.
To have your home in a place.

texts.title: My family
paragraphs: Hi! I'm Eva. This is my family. We are a small family. We live in Varna.
This is my mom. Her name is Nina. She is a doctor. This is my dad. His name is Peter. He is an engineer.
This is my brother, Dan. He is twelve. He is a student. I'm a student too.
My grandmother is seventy. She is very kind. My parents are very kind too.

objective.bg: Да представиш някого с "This is my…".

explanation.en: We introduce people with "This is my…": This is my brother. English uses "my" before the person, while Bulgarian often puts it after: "брат ми".
explanation.bg: Представяме хора с "This is my…": This is my brother. На английски "my" е пред думата, а на български често е след нея: "брат ми".

items.sentence: This is my mother. ___ is a doctor.

explanation.en: "Mother" is a woman, so we say "she". English needs this pronoun: in Bulgarian "Лекарка е" is fine, but in English you can't say "Is a doctor".
explanation.bg: "Mother" е жена, затова казваме "she". В английския това местоимение е задължително: на български "Лекарка е" е нормално, но на английски не може "Is a doctor".

hints.en: Is a mother a man or a woman?
hints.bg: Майката мъж ли е или жена?

items.prompt: Dan is ten. ___ (= Dan's) sister is Eva. Choose the word for the gap.

explanation.en: Dan is a boy, so it is "his sister". In English, "his/her" agrees with the owner (Dan), not with the thing (sister). "He" is not a possessive, and "he's" means "he is".
explanation.bg: Dan е момче, затова е "his sister". На английски "his/her" се съгласува с притежателя (Dan), а не с предмета (sister). "He" не показва притежание, а "he's" значи "he is".

hints.en: Who does the sister belong to — a boy or a girl?
hints.bg: На кого е сестрата — на момче или на момиче?

hints.en: Think about the owner, not about the sister.
hints.bg: Мисли за притежателя, а не за сестрата.

objective.en: Use "her" for something that belongs to a woman.
objective.bg: Да използваш "her" за нещо, което е на жена.

items.sentence: Anna is a teacher. ___ (= Anna's) brother is a doctor.

explanation.en: Anna is a woman, so we say "her brother" — even though a brother is a man. "His" or "her" depends on the owner.
explanation.bg: Anna е жена, затова казваме "her brother" — въпреки че братът е мъж. "His" или "her" зависи от притежателя.

hints.en: Whose brother is it — Anna's. Is Anna a man or a woman?
hints.bg: Чий брат е — на Anna. Anna мъж ли е или жена?

items.sentence: My parents are teachers. They ___ very kind.

explanation.en: With "they" we use "are": They are nice. The short form is "they're". "Is" is only for one person (he, she).
explanation.bg: С "they" използваме "are": They are nice. Кратката форма е "they're". "Is" е само за един човек (he, she).

objective.en: Choose "is" or "are" for one or more people.
objective.bg: Да избереш "is" или "are" за един или повече души.

items.prompt: My brother and my sister ___ students. Choose the word for the gap.

explanation.en: "My brother and my sister" are two people, so we use "are": "My brother and my sister are students." "Is" is for one person, and "am" goes only with "I".
explanation.bg: "My brother and my sister" са двама души, затова използваме "are": "My brother and my sister are students." "Is" е за един човек, а "am" е само с "I".

hints.en: How many people are in the subject?

items.prompt: Talk about your mom's job. Which sentence is correct?

explanation.en: In English we say "She is a doctor" — with "a" before a job. In Bulgarian "Тя е лекарка" has no article, so learners often forget "a". "Is a doctor" has no subject, and "She a doctor" has no verb.
explanation.bg: На английски казваме "She is a doctor" — с "a" пред професията. На български "Тя е лекарка" е без член, затова често се забравя "a". "Is a doctor" няма подлог, а "She a doctor" няма глагол.

hints.en: Look at the small word before the job.

objective.en: Make a negative sentence with "is not".
objective.bg: Да направиш отрицателно изречение с "is not".

explanation.en: To make a sentence negative, put "not" after "is": He is not a teacher. In speech: "He isn't a teacher" or "He's not a teacher".
explanation.bg: За отрицание слагаш "not" след "is": He is not a teacher. В разговор: "He isn't a teacher" или "He's not a teacher".

objective.en: Find someone's job in a text.
objective.bg: Да откриеш нечия професия в текст.

explanation.en: Eva writes: "This is my mom. Her name is Nina. She is a doctor." Peter, her dad, is the engineer.
explanation.bg: Eva пише: "This is my mom. Her name is Nina. She is a doctor." Инженерът е Peter — баща ѝ.

hints.en: Find the sentence about Eva's mom.
hints.bg: Намери изречението за майката на Eva.

objective.en: Find a detail about a family member.
objective.bg: Да откриеш подробност за член на семейството.

items.sentence: Dan, Eva's brother, is ___ years old.

explanation.en: Eva writes: "This is my brother, Dan. He is twelve." Seventy is her grandmother's age.
explanation.bg: Eva пише: "This is my brother, Dan. He is twelve." Seventy е възрастта на баба ѝ.

objective.en: Find a detail about a family member.
objective.bg: Да откриеш подробност за член на семейството.

items.prompt: In the text, who is seventy?

explanation.en: Eva writes: "My grandmother is seventy. She is very kind." So the grandmother is seventy (70). Dan is twelve.
explanation.bg: Eva пише: "My grandmother is seventy. She is very kind." Значи бабата е на седемдесет (70). Dan е на дванадесет.

explanation.en: With "we" we use "are", like with "you" and "they": We are from Bulgaria. Short form: "we're".
explanation.bg: С "we" използваме "are", както с "you" и "they": We are from Bulgaria. Кратка форма: "we're".
